title: Time to event (censoring)
request: Let DCLab solve how-long-until problems where many rows have not ended yet: subscriptions that may still cancel, machines that may still fail.
spec: A survival kind: a duration and an event flag (censoring), a start moment; Kaplan-Meier and Cox baselines, gradient-boosted survival and discrete-time classification; C-index, integrated Brier score and time-dependent AUC at named horizons; checks for durations measured past the moment and for treating censored rows as events. Done when the replica (subscriptions with right-censoring) is solved, a model that drops censored rows is shown to be biased against the honest one, and survival curves per group are in the final record.
plan: Write the estimators in dclab_core with numpy, pandas and scikit-learn only: Kaplan-Meier, a ridge Cox fit by Newton-Raphson with Breslow ties, and discrete-time hazards on person-period rows.
Score with censoring: Harrell's C-index, inverse-probability-of-censoring weighted Brier and time-dependent AUC.
Build a replica where the truth is known: Weibull lifetimes, signups over two years, censored where the data ends, two columns counted during the follow-up.
Add the kind as a library kind (refused by the engine, partial in the matrix), with acceptance decisions judged against the replica's truth.
Review, fix, and show each test fails on the fault it guards.

decisions.decision: Training rows are censored at the holdout's first day, and the rows a model is fitted on at the validation cut.
decisions.why: A time split by start is not a time split if training rows keep outcomes dated after the holdout begins: a shock in the last months is learned from the future.

decisions.decision: The censoring weights come from the scored rows' own censoring.
decisions.why: The latest starts are censored early and heavily; weights from older rows are about 1 there, and the Brier score came out a third too low with the model order flipped.

decisions.decision: A column is counted during the follow-up only if it moves with the duration among rows still going and among rows that ended.
decisions.why: Among rows still going the duration is the calendar; a column known at signup that trends with the calendar moves with it too, but not among rows that ended.

decisions.decision: An export with no row still going is refused.
decisions.why: With no censored rows the durations of the rows that did end are a biased sample, and the checks for counted columns have nothing to compare.

change: dclab_core/survival.py (kaplan_meier, censoring_bias, censoring_check, duration_check, Cox, DiscreteTime with read_discrete, c_index in blocks, censoring_weights, brier, integrated_brier, auc_at, censor_at, evaluate), dclab_core/replicas/subscription_lifetimes.py, dclab_rnd/kinds/time_to_event.py, tests/test_core_survival.py, dclab_core/CHANGELOG.md, dclab_rnd/kinds/capability.json.

findings.defect: Training rows kept outcomes dated after the holdout's first day.
findings.scenario: On the replica 1158 training rows had an outcome after the cut; with a planted shock from day 560 (discount customers leaving), the holdout C-index was 0.69 for Cox as built and 0.51 when training was read only up to the cut.
findings.cause: The split ordered rows by start but kept every training row's full follow-up.
findings.fix: censor_at: training durations stop at the holdout's first day and events after it have not happened; the rows a model is fitted on stop at the validation cut.
findings.test: test_training_reads_no_outcome_after_the_holdouts_first_day (a different future for the training rows changes no score)
findings.impact: A change in the last months would have been reported as a model's skill.

findings.defect: The censoring weights were taken from the training rows and were about 1 on the holdout.
findings.scenario: At 90 days the training censoring curve was 1.0 and the holdout's 0.47; the Cox Brier score was reported 0.081 against a true 0.129, and the logistic model looked worse than Kaplan-Meier when it was better.
findings.cause: G was fitted on the rows the models were fitted on.
findings.fix: G is the Kaplan-Meier of the scored rows' censoring.

findings.defect: Dropping censored rows was never tested on a model.
findings.scenario: Fitting every model on the event rows only, or with every row an event, passed every test and the acceptance.
findings.cause: The bias was shown only on the curve without covariates, and the holdout was scored where training had no censoring.
findings.fix: The chosen model is also fitted the two wrong ways; its mean survival is compared with what the held-out rows show; the acceptance needs a gap of 0.05.

findings.defect: The discrete-time survival inside an interval was the previous interval's.
findings.scenario: Mean survival at 30 days was 1.000 against Kaplan-Meier's 0.956; at 600 days it was the value at 403.
findings.cause: A step read-out of interval ends.
findings.fix: A constant hazard inside each interval, continued past the last edge.

findings.defect: A column written at the end passed as a feature, and a failed censoring check was ignored.
findings.scenario: A cancel_reason filled only for cancellations stayed a feature (C-index 0.93); an export of ended rows only kept months_billed as a feature (C-index 0.94).
findings.cause: Only numeric columns among censored rows were tested, and solve did not read the censoring check.
findings.fix: A column filled or given a value only for ended rows is written at the end; an export without rows still going is refused.

findings.defect: A column known at signup that trends with the calendar was dropped.
findings.scenario: A list price rising every month was flagged, because among censored rows the duration is the calendar.
findings.fix: Flag only when the column also moves with the duration among ended rows, with the same sign.

findings.defect: The time split sorted text, cut inside a day with timestamps, and crashed on one start value or no events.
findings.scenario: Dates as dd/mm/yyyy made the holdout span two years; times of day put one day on both sides; one start value raised IndexError.
findings.cause: The start column was not parsed and edge cases were not refused.
findings.fix: Parse dates, cut on the day, and raise a clear error when a part is empty or has no event.

findings.defect: Horizons past the follow-up returned the last known survival.
findings.scenario: At 1000 and 5000 days Kaplan-Meier reported 0.101, though the longest duration was 728.
findings.cause: The step function was read beyond its data.
findings.fix: None past the longest duration followed.

findings.defect: The 'holdout read once' acceptance could not fail.
findings.scenario: Choosing the model on the holdout still passed: the check only echoed the start column's name.
findings.cause: It checked an argument, not the result.
findings.fix: It checks the holdout starts after every training row and that the chosen model is the validation's best.

findings.defect: Many estimator faults passed the tests.
findings.scenario: A Cox risk set without ties, a tie-free Breslow hazard, a shifted read-out, curves from the holdout, an unnormalised integral and ties counted concordant all passed.
findings.fix: Hand-worked tests of Cox with ties (baseline hazard, and the partial likelihood's gradient at the fit), the read-out, Brier, AUC and their integral, and the design.

findings.defect: The kind was detected for delivery-time questions.
findings.scenario: 'How long until the order is delivered?' read as time to event.
findings.fix: Only with an ending that can still be to come (cancel, leave, fail, default).

findings.defect: The kind named an evidence track that does not exist.
findings.scenario: /api/kinds advertised research/time-to-event/, which agents could not cite.

outcome: Built as a library and accepted on the replica (7 decisions); refused by the engine and partial in the matrix until the engine runs it.
lessons: A split by start time still leaks if the training rows keep outcomes dated after the cut: censor them at it.
Censoring weights belong to the rows being scored; the latest rows are censored differently from the oldest.
To tell a counted column from a calendar trend, look at the rows that ended too.
A replica that keeps the true lifetimes lets a test check the score itself, not only the ranking.
risks: Outcomes after the holdout cut read in training.
Censored rows dropped or counted as events.
Columns counted during the follow-up used as if known at the start.
Scores weighted by the wrong censoring.
